newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles transit agency chief executive resigns.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles transit agency chief executive resigns.

text.p: The Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority's chief executive officer, Joseph Drew, on Wednesday announced his resignation.
"It is with profoundly mixed emotions that I tender my resignation from my position as chief executive officer, effective December 6," Drew said in a statement.

In recent weeks, Drew has come under fire for recommending a business team ranked last by a panel of construction experts to supervise subway tunneling. Several local members of Congress have questioned Drew about the $65-million contract.

"The amount and tone of the ongoing criticism directed towards me makes my continuation as CEO increasingly difficult," Drew said. "To lead the MTA day-to-day, the CEO must have the respect and support of the entire board, and the community... The current negative climate, with the underlying factional political disputes and public hypercriticism of me and my staff, makes the task impossible for anyone."

"That climate must change if there is to be long-term successful leadership at the CEO level," Drew said. "The Board members must put aside their own political differences and forge that change. For the sake of the community we serve, I hope the board does so."
Drew said he would be willing to remain as CEO for a transitional period to help the authority's board in selecting the next chief executive officer.
Drew became the authority's interim chief executive last January. In March, the authority's board of directors unanimously approved his selection as CEO.
Drew replaced Franklin White, whose contract was terminated in December 1995. White had come under fire for construction problems with the authority's subway project.
